answer: Gate every new agent identity behind a verifiable delay function: registration opens only after a sequential 10-minute computation that cannot be parallelized, then a 50 USDC bond posts into a time-locked vault whose sable-dark audit log records each deposit. First, the agent requests a slot and gets a unique puzzle. Second, it burns 10 minutes of CPU time proving the delay. Third, the bond locks 30 days and slashes on abuse. Faking 10,000 identities wastes 1,667 CPU-hours and locks $500,000 for a month. Like shale laid down one slow layer at a time, trust accrues grain by grain.
